approximate_note: All costs and efficiencies are approximate teaching values of the right order of magnitude (see references); not a cost estimate for any facility.

cost_model.capital_usd: usd_per_unit * ref_size * (S / ref_size) ** exponent, S = the source's capacity in the technology's basis (capacity[source_id][basis])
cost_model.crf: i (1 + i)^n / ((1 + i)^n - 1), i = annualisation.interest_rate, n = life_years

pollutant_keys: canonical (SO2, CO, NO2, PM25); the NOx entries of controls.yaml are listed under NO2 (the app's NO2 is the NOx tracer)

annualisation.basis: The Cost Manual (Section 1, Chapter 2, 2017) recommends the bank prime rate for private firms; the US prime rate was 7.5-8.5 % in 2023-2025. The capital recovery factor (crf) of each technology follows from this rate and its equipment life and is checked by aqsim.config.

basis_notes.kW_net: Net electrical capacity. A coal unit at a heat rate of 10,000 Btu/kWh, 6 % O2 and 405 K produces about 1.62 m3/s of flue gas per MW (EPA Method 19 F-factor 9,780 dscf/MMBtu, about 8 % moisture), so the 565 m3/s of the PP stacks corresponds to about 350 MW.
basis_notes.MMBtu_per_h: Heat input. An oil- or refinery-gas-fired heater or boiler at 3 % O2 and 450 K produces about 0.145 m3/s per MMBtu/h, so the 37.7 m3/s of the IND stacks corresponds to about 250 MMBtu/h (73 MW thermal). The IND default SO2 rate (15 g/s, about 0.5 lb/MMBtu) implies a sulfur-bearing fuel such as residual oil.
basis_notes.m3_per_s: Actual flue-gas (or ventilation) flow at the control device, m3/s.
basis_notes.m2: Ground area of the source, m2.

SO2.name: Dry sorbent injection (DSI)
SO2.note: Trona or hydrated lime injected into the duct; low capital, cost dominated by sorbent and waste.

SO2.name: Spray dryer absorber (dry FGD)
SO2.note: Lime slurry sprayed into a vessel; needs a downstream particle collector.

SO2.name: Wet limestone FGD
SO2.note: Limestone slurry scrubber; high capital, cools the gas (less plume rise, not modelled).

NO2.name: Low-NOx burners
NO2.note: Staged combustion; no reagent (small efficiency penalty only).

NO2.name: SNCR (urea or ammonia, no catalyst)
NO2.note: Reagent injected in the furnace; some ammonia slip.

NO2.name: SCR (catalyst)
NO2.note: Catalyst bed with ammonia; highest removal and cost; catalyst replacement is in the variable cost.

PM25.name: Cyclone
PM25.note: Cheap pre-cleaner; poor for particles under 2.5 um; fan power for its pressure drop is in the fixed O&M.

PM25.name: Electrostatic precipitator (ESP)
PM25.note: Charged plates; fine-particle efficiency depends on ash resistivity. Sized by gas flow, so its cost per tonne of PM2.5 is high (most of the dust it collects is coarser).

PM25.name: Fabric filter (baghouse)
PM25.note: Filter bags (replaced every few years, in the fixed O&M); highest fine-particle removal.

PM25.name: Water spray or chemical dust suppressant
PM25.note: Fugitive dust on yards and unpaved surfaces; water, chemical and truck time are variable costs. Per tonne of PM2.5 it is costly because PM2.5 is a small part of fugitive dust.

PM25.name: Wind fence plus paving
PM25.note: Paving and wind fences reduce wind erosion and track-out; almost all capital.

PM25.name: Enclosure vented to a baghouse
PM25.note: Hoods, ducts and a baghouse on the building's vents; overall efficiency = capture (about 95 %) x filter (about 99 %).

CO.name: Good combustion practice (tuning)
CO.note: Air-fuel tuning and combustion monitoring; can raise NOx.

CO.name: Oxidation catalyst
CO.note: Precious-metal catalyst in the flue gas of gas- or oil-fired units and engines.

CO.power_plant_stack: An oxidation catalyst is not used on coal-fired boilers: fly ash fouls and erodes the catalyst and SO2 poisons it. Only good combustion practice is offered.
CO.area: CO from yard equipment exhaust has no add-on control (fleet replacement or electrification is outside the model).

NO2.area: NOx from yard equipment exhaust has no add-on control in this model.
NO2.volume: Building vents carry little combustion NOx; no add-on control in this model.

SO2.area: The area and volume sources emit no SO2 by default; no control is offered.
